skill.name: python-venv-manager
skill.description: Manage Python virtual environments, dependencies, and project setup workflows with practical tool guidance.
skill.summary: Guides Python environment setup with venv, Poetry, Pipenv, pyenv, pip-tools, testing, Docker, and dependency workflows.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences and normal Python environment documentation. Confirmed risks remain for remote installer commands piped into shells, shell expansion of dependency files, xargs-based package installation, and examples that create local .env files with secret-like values.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands are piped directly into shell or Python interpreters.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell examples with download, checksum or signature verification, source inspection, and then explicit execution steps.

remediation.issue: Dependency migration examples expand requirements files directly into install commands.
remediation.suggestion: Parse requirements with a safe Python script or review generated package lists before running poetry add.

remediation.issue: The xargs requirements migration example can install unintended packages from unreviewed file contents.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid xargs for dependency files; generate an audited list and quote each argument safely.

remediation.issue: The .env example creates secret-like values in a local file.
remediation.suggestion: Use .env.example for placeholders and state that real .env files must stay untracked and locally protected.

content.value_statement: Python projects often fail because environments, versions, and dependencies drift across machines. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for creating reproducible Python setups.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create and activate Python virtual environments with venv and virtualenv.
Compares dependency tools such as Poetry, Pipenv, and pip-tools for common project needs.
Provides setup workflows for new Python projects, existing projects, and migration to Poetry.
Documents troubleshooting steps for import errors, dependency conflicts, SSL errors, and corrupted environments.
Covers testing, linting, formatting, pre-commit hooks, Docker integration, and security hygiene.
limitations: It is a documentation-only skill and does not validate commands before execution.
Some installation examples use remote shell installers that require manual trust review.
Version examples may become outdated as Python packaging tools change.
It cannot resolve project-specific dependency conflicts without inspecting the project files.

use_cases.title: Start a clean Python project
use_cases.description: Create a reproducible project structure with a virtual environment, dependencies, tests, and formatting tools.

use_cases.title: Standardize team environments
use_cases.description: Choose between Poetry, pip-tools, Pipenv, and pyenv for consistent development setup across a team.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot dependency problems
use_cases.description: Diagnose import errors, package conflicts, SSL certificate failures, and broken virtual environments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic virtual environment
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-venv-manager to show me the safest steps to create a virtual environment, activate it, install packages, and save dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a dependency tool
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare packaging options before starting a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-venv-manager to compare venv, Poetry, Pipenv, and pip-tools for my Python web service. Recommend one approach and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Fix dependency conflicts
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve broken installs or incompatible packages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-venv-manager to help debug my Python dependency conflict. Ask for the package files you need, then propose safe commands to inspect and resolve it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Poetry migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from requirements.txt to Poetry.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-venv-manager to plan a migration from requirements.txt to Poetry for an existing application. Include validation steps and rollback considerations.

output_examples.input: Set up a new Python CLI project with Poetry.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step setup plan covering Poetry initialization, dependency groups, pytest, formatting tools, and verification commands.

output_examples.input: My imports work locally but fail in CI.
output: Check which Python interpreter CI uses.
Verify the virtual environment is active.
Install the package in editable mode if using a src layout.
Run dependency checks before changing versions.

output_examples.input: Move a requirements.txt project to a locked workflow.
output_examples.output: A migration outline that backs up current files, imports dependencies, creates a lock file, and tests installation in a clean environment.

best_practices: Review installer commands before running them, especially commands downloaded with curl.
Use lock files or hashed requirements for production deployments.
Test dependency updates in a clean virtual environment before merging them.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts directly into a shell without inspection.
Do not install project dependencies into the global Python environment.
Do not commit .env files, virtual environments, or generated cache directories.

faq.question: Does this skill create virtual environments automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples that an agent or user may run after review.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers venv, virtualenv, Poetry, Pipenv, pyenv, pip-tools, pytest, pre-commit, and Docker examples.

faq.question: Is it safe for production projects?
faq.answer: Use it as guidance only. Review all commands, pin dependencies, and avoid remote shell installers in production workflows.

faq.question: Can it fix dependency conflicts?
faq.answer: It can suggest diagnostic and resolution steps, but it needs project files and test results for accurate fixes.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review commands that install packages, modify shell configuration, create .env files, or read dependency lists into shell commands.
